results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 59 aligned unit summaries match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph in spec order (the five callout entries match no spec paragraph and are recorded with null). Summaries for p08, p11, p51, p30 and p47 name both halves of the spec's compound controlling ideas.
Setting the Scene at Veldmark: The Barcelona Fake-Rental Ring ¶4: The second phrase (why the analyst worked by hand) explains the first; one idea, the late manual takedown.
The Threat Model: What Classifieds Fraud Looks Like ¶2: The reimbursement point is tied causally to the statistics ('explains why banks now ask'); one idea.
Vertical Differences ¶1: The opening sentence is a lead-in; the paragraph has one idea, that where money moves shapes the threat model.
Architecture: The Risk Scoring Service ¶11: Framed as one idea, the graph's two hard constraints, announced in the first sentence.

results.draft_locus: Back to Barcelona: What Day-One Action Would Have Required ¶2
results.quote: Hearthly Spain's move to the shared platform was brought forward to the first quarter of 2028.
results.finding: The outliner needed two phrases (counterfactual day-one outcome / migration brought forward). The migration sentence is presented as an unrelated fact rather than as Veldmark's consequence of the counterfactual, so the unit reads as two ideas; the spec's controlling idea allows tying it causally (what having the components would have changed, and what Veldmark therefore did). flowA A11 reports the same passage.

Every unit traces to a supporting claim: scene to F2/F3, threat model and verticals to F1, signals to F2, architecture to F3/F4, friction to F5, messaging to F1/F5, labels to F4, banks to F1/F4, back-to-Barcelona to F2-F4, trade-offs and Chief Architect's view to F5/F6, failure modes and questions to F1-F6, conclusion to the claim.

Each evidence item, table, figure and quotation is introduced or interpreted in the prose: Figure 1 by the four-bullet list, the typology table by p13, the vertical table by p51, the signal table by p14, the latency table by p22, the rules/models table by p24 (thin lead-in, the table carries the comparison), the rule quote by p27, Figure 3 by p29, the ladder table by p33-p34, the threshold table by p36 (formula and minimum at 0.5), Figure 4 by the reference design, the label table and Figure 5 by p41-p42, the Back-to-Barcelona table by p47, sourcing and timing tables by p48 and p50, the decision table by p54; UK Finance, Mercari and Ofcom quotations each stated with what they show.

Every transition_in is expressed at its boundary: e.g. elaboration 'Barcelona is one instance of a wider threat', cause_effect 'The architectural consequence is', contrast 'The design lesson from Barcelona is about the policy, not the detector', similarity 'Friction acts before an action completes ... the same way', contrast 'The loop learns from labels; fraudsters learn by probing the gate', end_of_previous sequence 'The design also forces choices.', conclusion_summary 'Ingrid's day-one question now has one answer seen from every section.' The p37 sentence is tangled and the Trade-offs bridge abrupt, but both express the declared relationship (reported under flow_is_followable).

Post level: both flow readers describe a problem-to-solution arc framed by the Barcelona case (scene, threat, signals, scoring, friction, messaging, learning, banks, return to case, then reference sections), matching the declared problem_solution pattern with large_to_small and grouping; neither would move any ## section.

The intro reader predicted the roadmap's sections in order (Barcelona; threat model and vertical differences; signals including stolen photos and actor graph; scoring service with real-time and batch, rules and models; step-up friction with a cost-model threshold; messaging controls; labels; banks and police; back to Barcelona; trade-offs, failure modes, Chief Architect's view, questions), the three owned terms, the off-platform nature of the fraud, and the evidence (UK Finance, OLX, Which?, Meta, Stripe, Airbnb, fictional Veldmark). All roadmap promises are predicted. Note: AC-2's expected still lists vertical differences after trade-offs (pending journal-spec edit per the decision log); the reader's order matches the roadmap and the draft.

The reader routes the photo match with an unrelated seller to risk scoring as a fraud signal, combines photo reuse, price, account age and verification into one listing score, links the accounts at creation through the shared device so cluster risk raises every member's score, opens one actor-level case, holds the remaining listings at the gate that evening, and has analysts write and shadow-test a rule within hours. Matches expected.

The reader chooses the threshold by minimizing the explicit weekly cost ((fraud reaching trigger - fraud stopped) x harm + genuine lost x value of a lost genuine account), lists the inputs (volume, share stopped, genuine abandonment, the two costs), assigns the cost of a lost genuine user to the marketplace general manager, abandonment to experiment, and says the threshold is revisited when fraud adapts. Matches expected.
